Tehran seeks roadmap to lift Iran-Iraq tourist exchanges to 5m
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
14:43:14 UTC
23:43:14 KST

Tehran seeks roadmap to lift Iran-Iraq tourist exchanges to 5m
TEHRAN – Iran is seeking to increase tourist exchanges with neighboring Iraq to five million visitors in each direction within a year, Iran’s tourism minister said, calling for the goal to be turned into a detailed and measurable roadmap.
Tourism Minister Seyyed Reza Salehi-Amiri made the remarks at a meeting on expanding tourism ties with Iraq attended by ministry officials, representatives of the border provinces of Ilam, Khuzestan, Kordestan, Kermanshah and West Azarbaijan, and private-sector tourism operators.
“About 3.6 million Iraqi tourists currently travel to Iran, while around 3.5 million Iranians travel to Iraq,” Salehi-Amiri said, adding that the target should be to raise the figure to five million visitors in each direction within a defined timeframe.
He stressed, however, that massive Arbaeen pilgrimage should be separated from conventional tourism statistics.
Arbaeen distinct from conventional tourism
Salehi-Amiri said the annual Arbaeen pilgrimage is fundamentally different from conventional tourism because it is a largely popular, spontaneous and religious movement in which standard tourism components such as accommodation and paid services do not necessarily apply.
“Arbaeen is an ideological and popular movement,” he said, arguing that tourism policy should instead focus on travel that involves planned stays, tourism services and economic and cultural value creation.
He called for bilateral tourism ties to expand beyond religious travel to include medical tourism, leisure, shopping, cultural, academic and other forms of travel.
The minister noted that many Iraqi visitors to Iran travel beyond religious destinations such as Mashhad to cities such as Shiraz and Isfahan, demonstrating the broader potential of the Iranian tourism market for Iraqi travelers.
He urged the production of professional and targeted promotional content to introduce lesser-known attractions in both countries, including their historical, cultural, natural and medical tourism resources.
Transport and medical tourism
Salehi-Amiri said facilitating road and private-car travel should be a priority, arguing that easier border procedures for families and motorists could unlock significant untapped demand.
He also called for an assessment of airline capacity between the two countries, alongside the development of ground transport, shuttle services from Iraqi cities to Iranian tourist destinations and smoother border crossings.
Medical tourism was identified as another key area for cooperation. Salehi-Amiri said the sector had faced challenges because of the absence of an integrated system linking patients and travelers from their point of departure to their destination.
He said Iran had worked over the past two years to improve coordination among relevant agencies and was moving toward launching a comprehensive medical tourism system.
The proposed system, he said, should improve transparency, reduce intermediaries and coordinate services for medical travelers.
He also highlighted the need to address banking and currency problems, intermediary activities, communications and SIM-card access and other obstacles faced by foreign medical tourists.
Call for joint tourism mechanism
The minister proposed establishing a permanent mechanism for tourism cooperation between the two neighboring countries, saying the two sides should develop a common document outlining tourism capacities, challenges, obstacles and possible solutions.
He suggested establishing a joint supreme tourism council, a specialized working group and a joint office to hold regular meetings, follow up on decisions and assess progress.
Salehi-Amiri also called for joint tourism and handicrafts exhibitions, saying tourism could help drive economic development in border regions.
He added that organizing religious, medical, leisure and other forms of tourism within a coordinated framework could generate economic benefits while strengthening social and cultural ties between the two peoples.
One-year roadmap
Salehi-Amiri said the five-million target should be translated into a practical program with a timetable, designated responsibilities, performance indicators and monitoring mechanisms.
“We need to take the Iraqi prime minister’s proposal seriously and determine through clear planning how we can reach the five-million-tourist mark within the next year,” he said.
He added that the roadmap should assess several factors simultaneously, including regional security conditions, airline and ground-transport capacity, border infrastructure, medical, religious and leisure tourism, family and private-car travel, length of stay, accommodation and tourism-service infrastructure, and the role of the private sector.

China says will safeguard its own interests as US expands Iran sanctions
China, a key customer of Iranian oil, has advocated for a ceasefire, insisting US sanctions will not resolve the conflict.
China has said that it would safeguard its interests after Washington unveiled new measures while laying out plans for the “economic asphyxiation” of Beijing’s economic partner Iran.
Speaking at a regular news briefing in Beijing on Tuesday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian rejected Washington’s expanding pressure campaign, calling for an immediate end to unilateral measures.

“Cooperation between China and Iran has always been conducted within the framework of international law and should not be interfered with or disrupted,” Lin said.
“China has already stated many times that it firmly opposes illegal unilateral sanctions … China will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own rights and interests.”
The latest comments come nearly six months into the US-Israel war on Iran, as the United States rolls out new penalties on entities including several in China.
Washington also expanded secondary sanctions threats, urging governments worldwide to join its economic campaign.
Asked on Monday whether Chinese banks would be targeted by the new penalties, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said, “No one is above the reach of US sanctions.”
China has advocated for a ceasefire, insisting US sanctions will not resolve the conflict.
Beijing remains a key customer for Iranian oil and is directly affected by the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran has weathered sanctions for decades, using complex international financial networks to evade restrictions. Before the war, it continued to export millions of barrels of oil, mostly to China.
‘We will see a lot of resistance’ from China
Amid the US’s latest move, some analysts say threats to sanction Chinese entities over trade with Iran are unlikely to materialise. This is due to a combination of diplomatic and legal obstacles, according to Trita Parsi, executive vice president of the Washington-based Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft.
“If the US now goes after the Chinese only weeks before [Chinese President] Xi [Jinping] is supposed to arrive in Washington, I find it unlikely,” Parsi told Al Jazeera, pointing out that Washington faces significant friction on both fronts.
Diplomatically, Parsi pointed out that Beijing helped avert a severe economic crisis during the height of the war by halting its oil purchases just as prices spiked, cratering demand and keeping crude under $100 per barrel for extended periods.
“They did this because the Chinese objective was to make sure this crisis would not bring about a global recession, which would be bad for China,” Parsi said, suggesting the move indirectly spared Washington from an energy shock that would have hurt the US economy.
Beyond that, Beijing is unlikely to accept US attacks on its companies or economic interests without pushback. “I suspect that we will see a lot of resistance from the Chinese if the US actually ends up going after Chinese companies,” Parsi said.
Separately, the president of the Iran-China Chamber of Commerce and Industries, Majidreza Hariri, also criticised US policies, warning that Washington has entered into an economic war with Tehran.
“What Trump has said makes it clear that he has entered into an economic war with us and considers it a new phase of military and security wars!” Hariri wrote in a post on X.
“With this same reasoning, all of America’s economic targets and its partners around the world, and especially in the region, are considered military targets of the enemy and are targetable!”

CIA Director Arrives in Moscow for ‘Meetings,’ Reports Say
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
14:31:00 UTC
23:31:00 KST

CIA Director John Ratcliffe arrived in Moscow on Tuesday aboard a U.S. military transport plane, Axios and CBS News reported, with sources familiar with the trip saying that the intelligence chief is slated to hold a series of “meetings” in the Russian capital.
News of the rare visit broke just hours after the Kremlin told journalists it had no information about a Boeing C-17 Globemaster landing at Moscow’s Vnukovo Airport.
Flight-tracking data from Flightradar24 showed the large U.S. military transport plane flew from Joint Base Andrews near Washington, D.C., stopping in Riga, Latvia, on Aug. 23 before continuing to Moscow on Tuesday.
U.S. officials have not officially commented on the visit. The U.S. Embassy in Moscow did not respond to a request for comment.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov later confirmed the visit in remarks to The Washington Post, saying the purpose of Ratcliffe’s trip was for “contacts between security services.” He did not provide further details.
An anonymous source told The Kyiv Independent that the United States asked Ukraine to halt its strikes on Moscow and St. Petersburg ahead of Ratcliffe’s trip. The source said Ukraine would be briefed on the American intelligence chief’s meetings in Russia.
The last time a CIA director visited Russia was in November 2021, just months before President Vladimir Putin ordered the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. At that meeting, former Director William Burns met with Nikolai Patrushev, who was then serving as secretary of Russia’s Security Council.
Since his appointment in January 2025, Ratcliffe has maintained regular contact with his Russian counterpart, SVR chief Sergei Naryshkin.
Ratcliffe’s visit marks the first known trip to Russia by a senior American official since U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with President Vladimir Putin in January to discuss Ukraine peace negotiations.
U.S. President Donald Trump has vowed to broker an end to Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine. However, the American president has struggled to bring Moscow and Kyiv toward a compromise, as both sides ramp up airstrikes deep inside each other’s territory this summer.
In July, sources told Politico that FBI Director Kash Patel was also planning a trip to Russia later this year.

Sex sells and wins votes – and the Democrats know it | Arwa Mahdawi
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
14:30:25 UTC
23:30:25 KST

Despite being a card-carrying member of the International Order of Confirmed Homosexuals, I have spent quite a lot of time lately thinking about Abdul El-Sayed’s biceps. I mean, have you seen them? The progressive Michigan senate nominee is jacked and he knows it. He almost always wears a tight black T-shirt to show off his muscles and incorporates a lot of fitness content in his campaign.
I’m not the only one who has noticed El-Sayed’s prominent muscles. They have had a lot of coverage, and are seen as part of a wider attempt to rebrand the Democratic party. Which, I don’t need to tell you, has a serious image problem; a poll in March found that the party is looked on even less favourably than the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency. So, to make it look less like a party that is full of out-of-touch technocrats who sound as if they are reading from a 500-page PowerPoint presentation every time they try to explain anything, Democrats seem to be trying to up the sex appeal.
“Democrats enter their thirst trap era,” News website Axios recently declared, summing up the phenomenon. The piece observed that the Democrats’ main TikTok page has given “the thirst trap treatment” to big names including El-Sayed, Zohran Mamdani and senator Jon Ossoff (“nicknamed ‘Senator My Boo’ by internet fans”), by posting flirty photos and videos. Axios quotes a political analyst who explains that while female Democrats such as Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez have had their share of screen time, the Dems’ TikTok page has made a “very intentional choice to feature the most attractive male members”.
Fox News would appear to reluctantly agree with the assessment that Democrats are leaning into good looks to win the midterms. “El-Sayed is out in these tight T-shirts,” Fox News host Ainsley Earhardt said in a discussion last week. “AOC with her pretty smile. She’s beautiful. She’s got the red lipstick. You have Mamdani, always smiling … It doesn’t make their philosophy any less dangerous, right?… even with a tight T-shirt, it’s still socialism and it fails.”
Over on CNN there was a little more jubilation about the Democrats’ vibe shift. “Dems are hot again,” strategist Yemisi Egbewole proclaimed. “They’re coming out of the closet as hot people and I’m so excited.” Egbewole added that it wasn’t just about physical attractiveness: “I think they’re learning from Trump. Entertainment really sells.”
Sex sells too: it’s well established that voters around the world prefer good-looking candidates. But, while we may all be shallow deep down, some of us are shallower than others. A 2016 study found that rightwing politicians in Europe, the US and Australia tended to be more attractive than their progressive counterparts. That’s partly because “low-information” conservative voters are particularly prone to choosing attractive candidates. “In low-information city elections, a beauty increase of one standard deviation attracts about 20% more votes for the average candidate on the right and about 8% more votes for the average candidate on the left,” an analysis of the study by the Washington Post noted. Which raises the question: if looks really are so important to low-information rightwing voters, how did we end up with Donald Trump as president? (Woke 1.0 is over, haven’t you heard? It’s OK to say things like this now.)
Social media may have brought a new visual element to politics, but the most famous anecdote about how looks can sway an election is almost 70 years old. In September 1960, 70 million Americans watched Richard Nixon debate John F Kennedy in the first nationally televised debate between presidential candidates. Nixon had been the favourite going in but he had just been in hospital for a couple of weeks and looked terrible. JFK, on the other hand, was tanned and rested and had good stage makeup.
You can quibble with the conventional wisdom that Nixon lost that election on looks, but it certainly played a part. In his memoir, Nixon wrote: “What hurt me the most in the first debate was not the substance of the encounter between Kennedy and me, but the disadvantageous contrast in our appearances. After the program ended, callers, including my mother, wanted to know if anything was wrong, because I did not look well.”
In short: if thirst traps are what it takes to get the US on a better path, then so be it. Jacked candidates in tight T-shirts may seem like a cheap trick, but even Nixon’s mother would agree that it’s a sound political strategy.
Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist

Ukraine mapped Russia’s Su-35 down to individual control units—and found 22 firms nobody has sanctioned
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
14:30:23 UTC
23:30:23 KST

Ukraine's military intelligence has named the Russian companies that build the Su-35S fighter jet and singled out those no country has sanctioned, according to the Main Intelligence Directorate of Ukraine's Defense Ministry (HUR). The unsanctioned suppliers make parts as ordinary as wheels and fuel-system units, and one of them helped develop the aircraft. Kyiv wants sanctions efforts synchronized across every link of Russia's military-industrial complex.
The 22 firms no one has sanctioned
HUR identified 79 companies in the Su-35S production chain. Of those, 22 face no sanctions from any country restricting Russia over the war. The agency highlighted three. Rubin Aviation Corporation supplies the aircraft's braking and non-braking wheels. Gidroavtomatika builds the AU46-05 control units inside the fuel system. The Oktava research institute carried out design and development work on the Su-35S itself.
What the rest of the network builds
The 79 firms develop and produce the engines and fuel system, the control, communications, and guidance systems, the electronic warfare suite, and the main aviation missiles the jet carries into the war against Ukraine. HUR set the data out in the "Components in weapons" section of its War&Sanctions portal. The page carries a rotatable 3D model of the aircraft whose parts open onto the firms behind them, alongside directory listings and a profile for each company.
Ukraine mapped Russia’s Su-35 down to individual control units—and found 22 firms nobody has sanctioned
Three sanctions regimes, loosely aligned
The gaps HUR points to exist because the restrictions are not one list. The EU legislates in packages, the US and other G7 states maintain their own designations, and Ukraine issues sanctions by presidential decree, each covering a different set of firms. Kyiv has spent years asking partners to synchronize those lists, and its own designations often run ahead of them. A company can therefore supply a frontline fighter and still trade freely under most of them.
Previously, HUR ran the same exercise on the Su-34, where a third of the production network was still unsanctioned. The same pattern shows up above the component level, with Russia's largest arms conglomerate covered by EU measures while hundreds of its subsidiaries are not, and Western machine tools still sitting inside Russian missile plants.

Rare tornado rips through southern France (VIDEOS)
A rare and violent tornado has run rampant through the village of Pomas in southern France, injuring 39 people, including two critically, and damaging around 300 homes, according to the local authorities.
The tornado struck the village in the Aude department on Monday evening, with footage showing a large funnel swirling over the settlement, with gusts of violent winds wreaking havoc, ripping apart roofs, and smashing windows.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez called it a “tornado of rare intensity” while praising firefighters, security forces, and volunteers involved in the response.
Rescue operations continued through the night, the prefecture said on Tuesday, with 75 firefighters deployed alongside specialist reinforcements to check damaged buildings and search affected areas.
Residents forced from their homes were sheltered in a multi-purpose hall with help from the Red Cross, while others were temporarily relocated with relatives or to neighboring communes.
🌪️Eyewitness footage recorded from the village of #Verzeille captured a #tornado forming and swirling beneath a violent supercell thunderstorm south of the southern French city of #Carcassonne. https://t.co/tL5GfNBnxLpic.twitter.com/oGurjJdrxi
📌Authorities reported at least 26… pic.twitter.com/U5AVlVP0iw
While no people were reported killed or missing, among the injured was a pregnant woman who was hurt when her house collapsed on her, according to AFP.
The storm also battered electricity infrastructure across southern France. Grid operator Enedis said about 21,000 households were without power across the south on Tuesday morning, including around 1,600 in Aude. The prefecture later put the number still without electricity locally at about 1,400.
The tornado appears unusually powerful by French standards. Emmanuel Wesolek, president of the Keraunos severe-weather observatory, told HuffPost that an initial assessment indicated “gusts of more than 200 kph” and potentially as high as 240 kph.
The tornado would likely rate somewhere between the upper end of EF2 and the lower end of EF3 on the Enhanced Fujita scale, he added.
According to Meteo-France, while not as frequent as in the US, a few dozen tornadoes occur in mainland France in an average year, and most are of low intensity. According to figures cited by HuffPost, EF2 tornadoes occur only once or twice annually, while an EF3 is recorded roughly once every four years.

UNRWA urges international community to protect training center after Israeli raid
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
14:29:13 UTC
23:29:13 KST

Serdar Dincel
25 August 2026•Update: 25 August 2026
The UN agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA) on Tuesday called on the international community to act “immediately and decisively” to safeguard its Qalandia Training Center north of Jerusalem after Israeli security forces raided the facility. 
“Today at approximately 10:00, Israeli Security Forces forcibly entered” the center in occupied East Jerusalem, UNRWA said in a statement. 
At least four armored vehicles entered the premises, accompanied by more than 50 Israeli security personnel, it added. 
Approximately 20 UNRWA staff members were present at the site at the time of the incident, the agency noted. 
“The entry of armed security forces into a United Nations facility, without the authorization or consent of the United Nations, is unacceptable,” it added. 
Earlier Tuesday, the Israeli army carried out raids in the village of Kafr Aqab and the Qalandia refugee camp north of Jerusalem, forcing agency staff to vacate the training center. 
Israeli forces also issued demolition warnings for several Palestinian structures in the area. 
Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir boasted about the raid on the training center, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had directly ordered the operation, contravening UN protections and international warnings. 
The raid came a day after representatives of 49 diplomatic missions accredited to the State of Palestine visited the center to assess conditions facing refugees and Israeli restrictions on the agency’s work. 
Ben-Gvir personally took part in the raid, posting a photograph of himself at the center’s entrance on social media and showing an Israeli flag that had been hoisted over the facility by Israeli forces. 
“UNRWA is in our hands,” Ben-Gvir crowed in the social-media post. 
The raid on the facility comes as Netanyahu’s government seeks to appease its far-right constituency amid mounting domestic political pressure, according to political observers. 
Netanyahu, for his part, said the evacuation of UNRWA staff from the center had been carried out on his direct orders. 
“In accordance with my directive and following the law we passed, the evacuation of the UNRWA compound in Kafr Aqab, Jerusalem, began today,” he said in a  statement. 
He added that his government would not allow UNRWA to operate and “will act against it by all means at its disposal.” 
Netanyahu’s actions come despite the fact that UNRWA facilities are protected -- in theory at least -- by rights and privileges granted to the UN under international law. 
Facility protected under international law 
Earlier this month, UNRWA said the Qalandia training center was a UN vocational training facility. 
It stressed that all the agency’s facilities, including the Qalandia center, were protected by UN privileges and immunities under international law. 
The agency noted that the center was established in 1952 as its first training center, adding that it provides technical and vocational training to about 340 young Palestinian refugees each year. 
At the beginning of 2025, Israel closed UNRWA’s main headquarters in the Sheikh Jarrah neighborhood of occupied East Jerusalem and later announced its seizure by the authorities. 
UNRWA was established in 1949 by a UN General Assembly resolution, and was tasked with providing assistance -- and extending protection -- to Palestinian refugees in Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe on secret trip in Russia
CIA Director John Ratcliffe is in Moscow, Russia, for meetings, sources familiar with the situation told CBS News on Tuesday.
News of his trip comes after a U.S. Air Force Boeing C-17A Globemaster III transport plane was spotted at a Moscow airport, along with a U.S. diplomatic motorcade. Neither the U.S. nor Russian governments has commented on the identity of the U.S. official in Russia or the purpose of the visit.
The CIA did not immediately comment.
It appears to be Ratcliffe's first known trip to Russia as CIA director, though he has maintained contact with Russian intelligence counterparts.
Ahead of Ratcliffe's trip, the U.S. told Ukraine that a senior delegation would be traveling to Moscow and asked it to suspend strikes until the delegation's departure, according to a senior Ukrainian official.
Ratcliffe's visit comes as recent U.S. intelligence assessments indicate that Putin's risk calculus may be shifting, with the Russian leader potentially increasingly willing to authorize provocative actions against NATO members — including hybrid operations and other deniable measures short of conventional military action — in order to test the resolve of the alliance and the Trump administration.
At this time, U.S.-mediated peace talks with Ukraine remain mostly stalled, with the sides still far apart on core issues.
The CIA has played a role in recent U.S.-Russia detainee exchanges, including the April 2025 release of a U.S.-Russian dual national Ksenia Karelina, whose case Ratcliffe personally negotiated. The agency was also involved in the 2024 prisoner exchange that secured the release of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich and Marine veteran Paul Whelan.
Former CIA Director William Burns traveled to Moscow in November 2021, when he met with senior Russian officials and spoke directly with President Vladimir Putin to warn him against invading Ukraine.

Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25

European Commission announces new decisions and defense payments for Ukraine in coming weeks
Ukrinform reported this, citing European Commission spokesperson Balazs Ujvari as saying at a news briefing in Brussels.
At the same time, he noted that the European Commission had not received an official request from Ukraine for the early disbursement of the allocated funding.
“We have allocated €45 billion for this year and around €45 billion for next year. This year, €28 billion is allocated for defense and around €17 billion for budget support, and this is also the plan for next year. As far as I know, we have not received an official request to accelerate this process. So, we are focused on implementing this plan,” the spokesperson said.
Of the €28 billion earmarked for Ukraine’s defense support this year, the EU has already allocated €22 billion, of which €8.5 billion has already been disbursed, the official went on to say.
“In the coming weeks, you will see more decisions, more payments. Over the next few weeks, we will be very busy on defense because we know what is at stake, we know there is an incredible sense of urgency, and accordingly, we are accelerating our work,” Ujvari said.
Asked whether the European Commission had rejected Ukraine’s request for early funding, Ujvari clarified that the EC had not received such a request. “We have not been informed bilaterally that Ukraine wants early funding, so we are focused on the plans we have in place,” he added.
At the same time, the spokesperson emphasized that the European Commission remained open to considering any requests from Ukraine.
“There is a continuous exchange of information between us and Ukraine about the latest developments. And we are ready to meet Ukraine’s requests to the maximum extent possible. But again, we have a plan that has been put in place, exchanges of information with Ukraine are ongoing, and we will conduct our work on that basis,” he explained.
Responding to a question about the contribution of other international partners toward covering Ukraine’s defense needs, Ujvari said that the EU’s contribution was significant but insufficient to fully meet Ukraine’s needs.
“That is why we use every opportunity to raise this issue with our partners, like-minded countries in the G7 and in ad hoc formats,” the spokesperson said.
He added that the EU was focused on implementing its share of the contribution to Ukraine’s defense, but “it is important that other partners also follow this example.”
For her part, European Commission chief spokesperson Paula Pinho praised several of Ukraine’s partners for their additional bilateral commitments and offers of defense assistance to Ukraine.
As previously reported by Ukrinform, President Volodymyr Zelensky said that the Coalition of the Willing summit in Kyiv on August 24 had resulted in an agreement to supply Ukraine with an unspecified number of missiles for Patriot air defense systems.

Ghislaine Maxwell loses bid to throw out conviction for aiding Jeffrey Epstein
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
14:22:02 UTC
23:22:02 KST

A US judge rejected Ghislaine Maxwell's bid to throw out her conviction and 20-year prison sentence for helping the late financier Jeffrey Epstein sexually abuse teenage girls.
In a decision made public on Tuesday, US District Judge Paul Engelmayer in Manhattan said Maxwell's claims were all meritless, and all or almost all were frivolous.
He said most were based on arguments Maxwell previously lost or failed to make in challenging her December 2021 conviction, while much of the supposedly "new" evidence disclosed this year through the Epstein Files Transparency Act was irrelevant.
"On the contrary, to the extent it is relevant, far from exculpating her, it incriminates her or reinforces the correctness of the legal rulings Maxwell challenges," Engelmayer wrote in a 67-page decision.
Engelmayer also called Maxwell's claim that prosecutors illegally withheld some evidence "conclusory, cynical, and wrong."
Maxwell represented herself. Engelmayer said an appeal "would not be taken in good faith," and the court would not pay her filing fees if she declared herself unable to afford it.
Jurors convicted Maxwell on five charges for recruiting and grooming underage girls for Epstein to abuse between 1994 and 2004, in a trial before a different judge.
Prosecutors called Maxwell's claims baseless, late
Maxwell had been seeking a writ of habeas corpus declaring her punishment unlawful.
Her petition represented the broadest effort by the former British socialite and Epstein girlfriend to overturn her conviction, the most significant successful prosecution to emerge from the Epstein scandal.
An earlier appeal by Maxwell focused on Epstein's non-prosecution agreement, which led to his 2008 guilty plea on a Florida state prostitution charge. The US Supreme Court rejected that appeal last October.
A spokesman for the US Attorney's office in Manhattan, which prosecuted Maxwell, declined to comment. Prosecutors argued that Maxwell's latest claims were baseless, filed too late, or failed to show her trial was unfair.
Maxwell called victims' lawyers 'de facto prosecutors'
In her latest challenge, Maxwell said many documents disclosed this year under the Epstein files law showed that lawyers representing Epstein's accusers served as "de facto prosecutors and agents of the government."
She also said prosecutors did no real investigating of their own, citing, among other things, their failure to interview Leslie Wexner, the retail billionaire behind Victoria's Secret who hired Epstein to manage his personal finances.
Wexner, 88, told Congress in February he severed ties with Epstein in 2007 and did not know about Epstein's crimes.
Maxwell also objected to alleged gaps in witness testimony, and alleged government suppression of potentially exculpatory grand jury testimony by a Palm Beach, Florida police detective about a green massage table at Epstein's villa there.
Epstein died at age 66 in a Manhattan jail cell in August 2019, five weeks after being arrested on sex trafficking charges. New York City's medical examiner called the death a suicide.
Maxwell is housed at a minimum-security federal prison camp in Bryan, Texas. She is eligible for release in July 2037, when she will be 75.

Acronis pushes AI beyond recommendations with new autonomous IT platform
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
14:22:02 UTC
23:22:02 KST

For the past two years, enterprise AI has largely been built around recommendations. It summarizes incidents, prioritizes alerts, and suggests what an IT technician should do next. The technician still makes the decision and still does the work.
Software vendors are now trying to move beyond that model. Rather than telling IT teams what should happen, the next generation of AI is beginning to carry out parts of the work itself.
The workload on IT professionals only grows as cyber incidents become more frequent. In Israel, 4,800 cyber incidents were recorded in June alone, nearly three times the number reported during the same month a year earlier. While government agencies and critical infrastructure remain major targets, smaller businesses are increasingly being affected as well, leaving IT teams with more incidents to investigate and less time to determine which pose the greatest risk.
As organizations look for ways to manage increasingly complex IT environments, software companies are beginning to push AI beyond recommendations. Acronis, a global provider of cyber protection solutions, is one of the latest enterprise software companies betting that autonomous execution, not better recommendations, will define the next phase of AI for IT teams. At its Acronis Accelerate: The Journey to Autonomous IT event, the company announced its new platform designed to bring agentic AI into MSP workflows.
Built around a unified workspace, the platform is designed to reduce the amount of manual coordination required to manage modern IT environments. Bringing operational data, service tickets, monitoring, and security into one system allows technicians to assess incidents from a single interface rather than piecing together information from multiple applications.
Part of a broader movement towards autonomous AI
The platform also reflects a broader move towards autonomous AI. Rather than stopping at identifying a problem, it can gather context around an incident and automatically begin handling certain routine tasks. MSPs can also build their own automated workflows and define which actions the platform can perform autonomously and which will continue to require human intervention.
Jan-Jaap Jager, CEO of Acronis, shares: “AI-native is not a marketing label for the company but a core design principle that guides how its products are built and operated, as well as how it helps partners manage and grow their businesses. The goal is to provide MSPs with a single environment where people and AI agents can collaborate securely, transparently, and at scale, and this year's product releases bring that vision to life.”
Israel one of Acronis' fastest-growing markets
Israel has also become one of Acronis’ fastest-growing markets, with cloud annual recurring revenue increasing 27% over the past year and adoption of its advanced EDR solution rising 37%. The country also plays an important role in the company’s global operations, with nearly half of Acronis’ Israel-based employees working in research and development.
As IT environments continue to grow, the challenge is becoming less about collecting more data and more about deciding what deserves attention first. The next phase of AI in enterprise IT may not be generating better recommendations, but reducing the amount of routine work technicians perform, giving IT teams more time to focus on the problems that still require human intervention.

What's included in the new US sanctions campaign to pressure Iran's economy? - explainer
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
14:22:01 UTC
23:22:01 KST

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced what his department called "an economic onslaught" against Iran on Monday that combined new sanctions with threats against Tehran's trading partners.
His statement stopped short of some of the most punishing sanctions and did not list specific countries that would be targeted, or when those penalties would take effect.
Here's a summary of actions he announced:
Pressing other governments to sever economic ties with Iran
The United States will set timelines for other countries to shut down economic activity with Iran and threatens unspecified actions if they do not comply.
Foreign entities that facilitate money laundering or sanctions evasion for Iran risk being cut off from the US financial system.
More types of economic activity with Iran may now lead to secondary sanctions on other countries, individuals or entities regardless of where they are located.
These newly listed activities include dealings in digital assets like cryptocurrency, technology, gold, aviation and shipping.
Sanctions on specific Iran-linked entities, individuals, vessels
The Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has added specific sanctions on nearly 60 entities, individuals and vessels that it says are enabling Iranian activity.
The new sanctions target the Iranian defense ministry's ballistic and nuclear procurement network, a cyber group the US says is behind attacks on its infrastructure, and the shipping, trading and financial network involved in Iranian oil sales.
OFAC has also suspended several licenses that previously allowed some remittance payments to Iran and Iranian access to the US cultural and academic system.
Entities, individuals involved in Iranian military procurement sanctioned
More than 20 of the new sanctions are targeted at entities and individuals in the Middle East and Asia that Treasury says are involved in financial and logistical support for Iranian nuclear research and missile development.
These include China-based companies that supplied what the Treasury considers dual-use items for a previously sanctioned Iranian technology institute.
Sanctions on individuals involved in cyberattacks to expand
The US is expanding sanctions on several previously sanctioned individuals, accusing them of involvement in cybercrime or threats to US national security.
Iran-linked oil industry assets sanctioned
New sanctions aimed at stopping Iran's oil exports include vessel brokers, bunkering service providers and financial intermediaries. These name several individuals and entities based in the United Arab Emirates and others in Singapore and Hong Kong.
The Treasury also identified five tankers as part of what it called a "shadow fleet" and listed them as "blocked property," meaning OFAC prohibits US nationals or people based in the United States from having any financial transactions with them.

Ads appear in the Moscow metro promising ‘alternative service’ with no front-line deployment. Recruits still sign standard military contracts.
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
14:19:29 UTC
23:19:29 KST

Ads appear in the Moscow metro promising ‘alternative service’ with no front-line deployment. Recruits still sign standard military contracts.
Advertisements for “alternative civilian service” have begun appearing near Moscow metro stations, the independent Russian news outlet Vot Tak reported, citing a reader who spotted the signs.
The human rights project Get Lost had already reported on August 17 that stands advertising alternative service appeared in the Moscow metro.
Vot Tak published a photo of the advertisement, which describes the service as including a one-time payment of 2.3 million rubles, a 5/2 work schedule, benefits, and exemption from mandatory conscription, and rules out deployment to a combat zone. The position is based in Naro-Fominsk, in the Moscow region.
The advertisements seek communications specialists, telecommunications engineers, IT specialists, and drivers. The organization Zashchitnik.rf placed the stands and ads in the metro; according to Vot Tak, it has actively promoted its services on social media since December 2024, acting as an intermediary for people signing contracts with the Defense Ministry.
A Vot Tak correspondent called the number listed in the brochure, posing as a prospective candidate. A Zashchitnik.rf representative said enrolling in alternative service requires signing a standard military contract. Asked whether that person could later be sent to the front, the representative said, “No, that can’t happen.”
Get Lost has said Russians have previously been lured into signing contracts disguised as alternative service. “If you’re told it’s “alternative service by contract,” “one-year service,” “training near Moscow,” “drones,” “air defense,” “computer work,” “not the front,” or a “3/3 schedule” — and you’re handed a contract to sign, that’s not AGS. […] AGS is never arranged through a contract with the Defense Ministry, a volunteer unit, BARS, or any other military structure,” the project wrote.
Alternative civilian service, known as AGS, is work performed “in the interests of society and the state” in place of mandatory military service. The Russian Constitution guarantees it to people whose beliefs or religion conflict with military service, as well as to some members of indigenous peoples with small populations.

‘100%’, ‘Energy Drink’, immunity claims: FSSAI flags 6 food firms
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
14:19:06 UTC
23:19:06 KST

FSSAI flagged 6 food companies for misleading claims on products like coconut oil, energy drinks, and baby food.
NEW DELHI: Claims that promise more, sound healthier or make a product appear superior have come under the scanner of the food regulator, with the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) flagging misleading claims by six food business operators (FBOs) and directing corrective action.The cases range from the use of “100%” on coconut oil and “Energy Drink” on a caffeinated beverage to claims around immunity, growth, digestion and nutrition in baby food, as well as health and nutrient-comparison claims.Mondelez India Foods Pvt Ltd was flagged over misleading health and nutrient comparative claims. It subsequently withdrew the claims and advertisements from e-commerce platforms.
Sapiens Labs was flagged over a misleading claim and, after submitting its response, withdrew the claim and advertisements.Vichi Agro Products Pvt Ltd, along with the concerned packer, was flagged over a misleading trade name and deleted the product from its platform.In a separate case, Amway India Enterprises Pvt Ltd, Delhi, was flagged over the use of “100%” in the name “100% Pure Coconut Oil”. The company said it had voluntarily removed the term from packaging and promotional material and discontinued old stock from sales channels.
Revised packaging without the claim has been finalised and is being rolled out progressively from September-October 2026.In Kerala, Juza Foods, Malappuram, was flagged over multiple claims for its baby food products, including claims relating to nutrition, immunity, growth, digestion and nutrient content, besides comparisons with other milk powders. The company acknowledged the violations and agreed to remove the misleading claims.
It also said its selling website had been shut and rectification completed, while steps were being taken for licence-related changes and an e-commerce licence.Amway India was also flagged separately over use of the term “Energy Drink” on a caffeinated beverage. The company accepted the observation and removed the term from its product range, website and promotional material. Updated packaging is to be introduced from the production cycle beginning August 2026.The cases highlight the kinds of claims and product descriptions that can come under FSSAI scrutiny, particularly when they could influence how consumers perceive a food product.

NATO Military Committee to discuss support for Ukraine in Denmark on 18-19 September
The NATO Military Committee, the alliance's highest military body, will meet at the chiefs of defence level in Copenhagen, Denmark, on 18-19 September to discuss follow-up measures from the NATO summit in Ankara, including further military support for Ukraine.
Source: NATO's press service in Brussels, as reported by European Pravda
Details: The NATO Military Committee will discuss support for Ukraine at a chiefs of defence-level conference on 18-19 September in Copenhagen.
"NATO's highest military authority, the Military Committee, will meet at the chiefs of defence level from 18 to 19 September 2026, in Copenhagen, Denmark. The Chair of the Military Committee (CMC), Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, will preside the meeting," NATO said.
The meeting will also be attended by Supreme Allied Commander Europe General Alexus Grynkewich and Supreme Allied Commander Transformation Admiral Pierre Vandier.
"Together, NATO's senior military leadership will reflect on the follow up from the NATO summit in Ankara, in particular by addressing the further strengthening of the alliance's collective deterrence and defence, innovation and technology, support for Ukraine," NATO's press service said.
Background:
- At the Ankara summit, NATO member state leaders agreed that the alliance would provide Ukraine with at least €140 billion in military support over 2026-2027.
- In particular, Germany's contribution to the two-year support package for Ukraine agreed at the NATO summit in Ankara will amount to around €23 billion, allocated in the federal budgets for 2026 and 2027 for military assistance to Ukraine.

FACTBOX: Aftermath of Ukrainian drone attack on Russian regions, 426 neutralized UAVs
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
08:34:02 UTC
17:34:02 KST

MOSCOW, August 26. /TASS/. On-duty air defenses intercepted and destroyed 426 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones over Russian regions overnight, the Russian Defense Ministry said.
The drone attack caused a fire at a Wildberries e-commerce logistics center in Kotovsk, Tambov Region, that covered more than 100,000 square meters.
Two people were killed after a private home caught fire following a drone crash in the Lipetsk Region.
TASS has compiled key information on the attack’s aftermath.
Scale
- Air defense systems detected and destroyed a total of 426 Ukrainian fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles over Russian regions between 8:00 p.m. Moscow time (5:00 p.m. GMT) on August 25 and 7:00 a.m. Moscow time (4:00 a.m. GMT) on August 26, the Russian Defense Ministry said.
- According to the Defense Ministry, drones were brought down over the Belgorod, Bryansk, Kursk, Oryol, Kaluga, Tula, Lipetsk, Voronezh, Tambov, Ryazan, Nizhny Novgorod, Volgograd and Rostov regions, the Moscow Region, the Krasnodar Region and the Republic of Crimea.
- Local authorities issued drone danger alerts from midnight to 8:00 a.m. Moscow time (5:00 a.m. GMT) in 11 Russian regions across three federal districts, according to TASS calculations.
- Governor Andrey Klychkov said 43 drones were destroyed over the Oryol Region overnight.
- About 40 Ukrainian drones were downed in Taganrog and seven districts of the Rostov Region overnight, Governor Yury Slyusar said.
- Governor Vladislav Shapsha reported that 27 drones were destroyed over the Kaluga Region overnight.
- Another 27 drones were detected and destroyed over Voronezh and eight districts of the region, Governor Alexander Gusev said.
- Tula Region Governor Dmitry Milyaev reported the destruction of eight Ukrainian drones.
Attack on Wildberries warehouse in Tambov Region
- The town of Kotovsk came under a massive Ukrainian attack overnight on Wednesday, Tambov Region Governor Yevgeny Pervyshov said.
- The drone strikes caused a fire at a Wildberries logistics center.
- The fire spread across more than 100,000 square meters, Pervyshov said.
- Earlier reports put the fire area at 40,000 square meters.
- Staff evacuated the facility immediately after the alarm sounded, which saved lives and prevented injuries, Pervyshov added.
- Preliminary reports indicate that a Wildberries employee suffered a concussion from the blast wave.
- The Tambov Region prosecutor’s office is overseeing the protection of citizens’ rights following the Ukrainian drone attack on Kotovsk, the agency’s press service said.
Aftermath
- A Ukrainian drone crash caused a house to catch fire at one of the cottage communities in the Tambov Region, Pervyshov said.
- A man and a woman suffered moderate injuries in a Ukrainian drone attack in a suburb of Voronezh, a city in central Russia, and received hospital treatment, Gusev said.
- The drone attack also set three outbuildings on fire in another district of Voronezh, but firefighters quickly put out the blaze.
- A man was injured when drone debris fell in the Tula Region, Milyaev said.
- A drone crash caused a private home to catch fire in the Lipetsk municipal district in western Russia, Governor Igor Artamonov said.
- A man and a 14-year-old child died in the fire.
- Two women were hospitalized and received all necessary medical care.
- The prosecutor’s office is overseeing the protection of victims’ rights following the attack near Lipetsk, its press service said.

China Focus: Chinese open-source AI solves Arabic dialect puzzle
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
22:06:48 CST
23:06:48 KST

BEIJING, Aug. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese researchers have unveiled an open-source text-to-speech artificial intelligence (AI) model that tackles the long-standing challenge of Arabic speech synthesis. The system covers more than 20 regional variants of the language under a unified technical framework.
The model, named Habibi, meaning "my dear friend" in Arabic, was developed by a team of Chinese research institutions, including Shanghai Jiao Tong University, and video-sharing platform Kuaishou.
Spoken by over 400 million people, Arabic has more than 30 regional variants with sharp pronunciation and vocabulary differences. Modern Standard Arabic is used almost exclusively as the official and literary form, while daily conversation relies on dialects from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Morocco and elsewhere, making unified modeling difficult.
Previous research focused either solely on Modern Standard Arabic or on single dialects. Before Habibi, no open-source text-to-speech system unified these dialects.
For Arabic speakers, dialect voice matters in daily life, said Mahitab Elbakry, an Egyptian news editor in her thirties.
"If my mother wants to use a chatbot to recommend recipes, it is natural for her to interact with it in her dialect," she said. Elbakry also cited online health inquiries, noting that using a dialect would be more accurate and reduce the risk of miscommunication.
"Services tailored to Arabic dialects could become increasingly convenient and widely adopted," she added.
But she noted that while AI products like ChatGPT offer interactive and generative services in Egyptian Arabic, high subscription fees limit access for many users.
The Habibi team has made everything publicly available, including all the model files, the code for training and running it, and the test data, making it "the first such release for a multi-dialect Arabic text-to-speech system," the team said in a paper posted on arXiv, an open-access preprint platform for academic research.
The researchers also claim the AI model can replicate a voice from a brief recording, with no advance training required.
Habibi is the latest example of deepening China-Arab AI collaboration. Chinese tech firms and institutions, including iFLYTEK and Huawei, have been working with Arab partners to advance speech recognition, develop AI models, and optimize dialect synthesis.
Open source has been a key feature of China's AI development. China has proposed the Global AI Governance Initiative and implemented the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good, aiming to lower barriers to global AI adoption and bridge the intelligence divide.
The approach has drawn international attention. Recently, several U.S. tech firms and institutions, including Microsoft, Nvidia and Hugging Face, issued a joint statement supporting open-weight AI models. Microsoft's AI Diffusion Report 2025 also noted that China's "DeepSeek's rise shows that global AI adoption is shaped as much by access and availability as by model quality."
Although the AI Habibi has not yet entered the market, the researchers said it has already surpassed a leading commercial model on major dialect tests, highlighting the competitiveness of an open-source solution.
"We have always been committed to supporting open source," said Chen Xie, a member of the Habibi team and an associate professor at Shanghai Jiao Tong University. "We believe in the power of openness and sharing." ■

HARARE, Aug. 25 (Xinhua) -- Zimbabwe's annual inflation rate of the local Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG) currency fell further to 2.9 percent in August from 3.2 percent in July, according to official data released Tuesday by the Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency (ZIMSTAT).
The month-on-month ZiG inflation rate remained stable at 0.1 percent in August, unchanged from the previous month.
In U.S. dollar terms, the monthly inflation rate dropped to 0.0 percent in August, down from July's 0.3 percent. The annual U.S. dollar inflation rate held steady at 3.1 percent, ZIMSTAT reported.

The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, the country's central bank, said last week that it expects annual ZiG inflation to average around 5 percent by the end of 2026, with monthly inflation staying under 1 percent due to a tight monetary and fiscal policy stance.
Zimbabwe recorded a single-digit annual ZiG inflation rate of 4.1 percent in January for the first time in over three decades, with monetary authorities reiterating their commitment to maintaining price stability to anchor long-term macroeconomic growth. ■

COLOMBO, Aug. 25 (Xinhua) -- Sri Lanka on Tuesday formally opened its 2026 offshore oil and gas licensing round, inviting international energy companies to bid for exploration acreage in the Mannar Basin as the government seeks to restart a petroleum exploration drive that has remained stalled for years.
The Petroleum Development Authority of Sri Lanka said bids are expected to close in the early part of 2027, after which proposals will be evaluated and qualified operators selected. Successful bidders will be awarded exploration blocks through Petroleum Resources Agreements before seismic acquisition and exploratory drilling begin.
The licensing round is expected to cover four exploration blocks in the Mannar Basin, where earlier drilling has already established the presence of a working petroleum system and natural gas accumulations.
Ceylon Petroleum Corporation Managing Director Mayura Neththikumarage said the authority would seek technically competent oil and gas companies capable of carrying out exploration safely and in an environmentally responsible manner.
Previous exploration has already confirmed natural gas discoveries offshore Sri Lanka. Exploratory drilling by Cairn Lanka in 2011 encountered hydrocarbons in the Mannar Basin, establishing that the basin contains an active petroleum system.
The next stage will require more detailed exploration to determine the location, size and commercial viability of prospective resources.
Minister of Labor and Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Anil Jayantha Fernando expressed confidence in Sri Lanka's oil and gas potential but acknowledged that exploration carried economic, environmental, social and geopolitical risks that would have to be managed as the program progresses.
The launch marks the latest attempt to attract international investment into the Mannar Basin after earlier exploration programs failed to progress to commercial production. ■

What is phubbing? The tech habit quietly damaging relationships
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
13:45:26 UTC
22:45:26 KST

As our digital footprints grow, questions about digital privacy and tech habits are becoming more common between couples.
"phubbing"Most of us use a variety of apps, social media platforms and scheduling tools as our lives become increasingly digital.
However, for couples, this can lead to interesting dynamics and questions. One of you may love being online and posting frequently on social media, whereas the other could prefer a quieter, more private lifestyle.
As such, how you approach technology and digital privacy as a couple could be completely different to how you handle it individually.
'Phubbing' on the rise
Unsurprisingly, technology can have both a positive and a negative impact on your relationship.
Phone snubbing, commonly known as "phubbing" and a related pattern called "technoference" are both increasingly common.
While "phubbing" refers to ignoring or snubbing a partner in favour of a phone, "technoference" refers to any interruption to couple activities caused by technology, such as constant calls, messages or notifications.
According to a 2025 study published in the journal Human Behavior and Emerging Technologies, survey respondents used their smartphones during 27% of the time they spent around their partner, on average.
Around 86% of respondents also used their phone every day while around their partner.
This was based on objective phone-tracking data rather than self-reports, which may not be as accurate.
The study found that phone use around one's partner could predict lower relationship satisfaction and co-parenting quality, as well as greater depression and lower life satisfaction. The effects were more pronounced for women.
On the other hand, technology can also benefit your relationship by making it easier to stay in touch, schedule important dates and activities, or bond over a favourite show.
When it comes to digital privacy, however, things can get more complicated. Couples today have to navigate a number of situations that did not exist for previous generations.
According to the relationship resource Love Respect, couples may need to discuss digital boundaries around privacy and exclusivity.
This can include whether it is okay to tag each other in pictures and posts or check in somewhere together. Whether to make a relationship status public is another point worth discussing, along with whether partners can follow each other's mutual friends.
However, one of the most important digital privacy questions couples may need to align on is whether they are comfortable using each other's devices.
Another major question is location sharing. According to a Civic Science report published last year, around 52% of Americans share their location with a spouse or partner.
In other cases, couples may disagree over home security and tech due to privacy concerns, as well as over what personal information to share online, for example when shopping, due to fears of scams.
Bridging the privacy gap
One of the first, if most obvious, things you can do when you realise you and your partner have different views on digital privacy is talk to them.
According to Love Respect, you should find out what they are comfortable sharing online while also communicating your own thoughts on what you want and do not want to share. Try to stay as calm and clear as possible.
It may help to discuss social media rules, such as tagging or posting photos of each other, or sharing relationship statuses. For location sharing, temporary sharing or turning off real-time tracking can ease friction.
You can choose to keep your phone and email passwords separate, as part of your personal autonomy.
It can also help to find small compromises, such as regular updates while travelling instead of an all-day live tracking app.
If the conversation is not progressing or is getting heated, it can help to take a break, give each other space and revisit the topic later, once both of you have had time to process things.
Approaching a couples counsellor can also help if you find it difficult to reach a satisfactory agreement.
Love Respect also emphasises that you should never feel pressured, manipulated or guilted into sharing your passwords or logins, or into changing digital habits you are comfortable with.

eHarmony misled Australians over 'free' subscriptions, court rules
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
13:45:13 UTC
22:45:13 KST

The Federal Court of Australia has ruled eHarmony misled Australian consumers with fake free dating services.
Users who paid for the website and app's one-month premium membership were charged for a six-month subscription and were unable to cancel payments that automatically renewed, even after profiles were deleted.
What's next?
The court will decide on penalties and consumer redress at a later date.
Users of eHarmony's website and app, the fourth largest of its kind in Australia, were misled with fake free dating services and then forced to pay, the Federal Court of Australia has found.
Users of its free basic membership were unable to talk to other single people online without paying, the court found.
Those who paid for a one-month premium membership were then charged for a six-month subscription, had to pay hidden and additional mandatory fees and were unable to cancel payments that automatically renewed, even after profiles were deleted.
"Try before you buy — and no pressure to sign up," a message on the free dating page read.
"We love our site and want you to enjoy it too, which is why we encourage you to sign up for free, review your matches and get to know us a little better."
It was a confusing statement, Justice Christopher Horan said on Tuesday when he found the company deceived its Australian customer base.
"I consider that such an assumption or conclusion was erroneous. Accordingly, the conduct was misleading or deceptive," he said.
"The one-month representation amounted to conduct that was liable to mislead the public.
"I accept the ACCC's submission that it was not possible to use the eHarmony Platform as a Basic member, free of charge, to 'date' other members by engaging in ongoing communications for the purposes of developing a romantic relationship."
The court found about 1.3 million users from Australia registered for a basic membership between 2019 and 2024.
One user who gave evidence to the court — and cannot be named for legal reasons — signed up for a six-month membership at a one-time discounted payment of $155.64, but deleted her profile two months later after failing to meet anyone.
When the six-month period expired, eHarmony renewed her subscription and billed her credit card $478.80.
She told eHarmony she didn't wish to continue her subscription and cancelled her credit card when the platform refused her request.
The company, which refers to itself as "the No.1 trusted dating app" referred the woman to a debt collection agency.
The proceedings were brought before the federal court after the consumer watchdog became aware of the repeated pattern.
The ACCC received hundreds of complaints from consumers, commissioner Luke Woodward said.
"Dating platforms are an important part of Australians' social lives,'' he said on Tuesday.
"Many people use them to meet others and form valuable connections.
"Consumers were not adequately informed about their memberships' duration or that the membership would automatically renew, including, for many, at a much higher price."
The court will decide on penalties and consumer redress at a later date.

One million Afghan children suffer ‘life-threatening’ malnutrition: UN
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
13:44:00 UTC
22:44:00 KST

One million Afghan children suffer ‘life-threatening’ malnutrition: UN
- One million Afghan children face life-threatening severe acute malnutrition amid a worsening crisis, with 3.7 million suffering from wasting, UNICEF warns.
- Hospital admissions for malnourished children have risen sharply, with southern hospitals overcrowded and many cases involving children under two years old.
- Aid cuts have closed over 100 treatment sites, leaving UNICEF's US$180 million nutrition programme only 22% funded, risking more child deaths without urgent action.
AI generated
Geneva – One million children in Afghanistan are suffering from life-threatening malnutrition in a worsening crisis sweeping the country, the United Nations warned on Aug 25.
Across Afghanistan, 3.7 million children suffer from wasting, meaning they are acutely malnourished, the UN children’s agency UNICEF said.
Among them are “one million children who are suffering from life-threatening severe acute malnutrition” – the worst form, said UNICEF’s Afghanistan country representative Tajudeen Oyewale.
“If there is no treatment, and we are not able to act fast, that one million number are at risk of dying,” he told reporters in Geneva, speaking from Kabul.
Afghanistan has endured repeated hunger emergencies in recent decades as it has struggled through civil war and other crises. An economic collapse followed the Taliban government’s return to power after US-led forces withdrew in 2021.
“Malnutrition plays a central role” in the growing numbers of deaths of very young children, Oyewale said.
Nearly 40 per cent of children admitted to hospitals with severe wasting and medical complications were babies under six months old, he said.
Meanwhile, children under two years old make up more than 80 per cent of severe acute malnutrition cases in Afghanistan.
He described a “worsening nutrition crisis” across the country, with more than half a million children admitted to hospital so far in 2026 for high-risk moderate and severe wasting.
In July 2025, around 6,000 severe acute malnutrition cases were admitted; in July 2026, the numbers went above 8,000 – a third higher.
“In parts of southern Afghanistan, some hospitals are now seeing three or four severely malnourished children for every available bed,” he warned.
‘Vicious cycle’
Oyewale said an “increasingly alarming picture” was developing, with families cutting back on nutritious food and meals becoming smaller.
Children’s first food beyond breast milk may be little more than bread with tea, or watered-down yoghurt, “and for a growing child, this is simply not enough”.
He said children could get trapped in a “vicious cycle”: being poorly nourished, developing severe diarrhoea or respiratory infections, and then in turn becoming more malnourished.
These problems are compounded by Afghanistan’s other troubles, such as successive years of drought, flash floods, regional instability and cross-border trade disruptions.
The return of six million Afghans from abroad since 2023 – more than half of whom are children – is also exacerbating the pressures on stretched resources.
While treatment for malnutrition can save lives, if survivors return home to the same conditions, “we frequently see those kind of children relapse and come back”.
Oyewale said that while the needs were increasing, services for children were being slashed due to international aid cuts.
He said more than 100 sites treating children for severe wasting had closed since 2025.
UNICEF’s nutrition programme in Afghanistan is estimated at US$180 million (S$228.5 million) in 2026 but is only 22 per cent funded.
“We should not wait until a child is dangerously thin and lying in a hospital bed before we act,” Oyewale said. AFP

Ukraine Tests World's First Purpose-Built Robot Aircraft Carrier for Drones
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-25
13:43:00 UTC
22:43:00 KST

A Ukrainian naval drone company unveiled the world’s first dedicated drone aircraft carrier on Monday, confirming months of reports that Kyiv’s military had developed a means of launching airborne strike drones from remote-controlled large motorboats.The 7-meter-long Magura MV11 marine drone was displayed and identified to the public during the Ukrainian Independence Day parade in a sail-by on the Dnipro River, the military information platform Oboronki reported.
The Ukrainian marine drone manufacturer UFORCE has produced Magura model boats since 2023. The motor-boat-resembling sea drones have for the most part been used by Ukrainian naval commandos for kamikaze strikes against Russian ships and shore infrastructure, and more rarely as platforms for special missions.
The MV11, per the Oboronki report, is Ukraine’s first publicly identified sea drone, designed from keel up, to carry and launch other unmanned systems from its onboard, “allowing the drone to act as a mobile naval base” – as a remote-controlled aircraft carrier/drone hanger.
Usable payload of the vessel as a mothership/transport platform is 2,200 kilograms (4,850 pounds). According to developers, the MV11 is capable of operating autonomously up to seven days. The article said the drone was developed jointly by UFORCE designers and R&D bureau in Portugal, with financing from unnamed Ukrainian allied states.
Russian Strikes Injure 35 Across 3 Cities, Including 2-Month-Old Infant
Photos and videos showed the vessel’s deck as a flat top broken into transport sections along the length of the hull, with doors protecting the transport section from sea and spray. The images run on major Ukrainian news platforms showed the compartments in a closed position.
Video published by UFORCE in March 2026 demonstrated a Magura launching an interceptor Unmanned Air Vehicle (UAV) emerging from a container mounted on the deck of a Magura-type robot boat. Ukrainian military information platforms have suggested drones carried in a launch compartment would need to be mechanically restrained in a cradle or rack to protect them from the sometimes-sharp sea maneuvers carried out by Magura pilots.
Given a typically sized Ukrainian first-person-view (FPV) drone armed with a conventional munition sufficient to destroy an armored vehicle, available deck space aboard an MV11 might be sufficient for quick launch of 20-40 aircraft in a single wave, and up to three waves of aircraft if the FPV drones were stored hopper-style in layers, Kyiv Post researchers found. The actual aircraft carrying capacity of the MV11 has not been made public.
According to UFORCE, the MV11, aside from an aircraft carrier configuration, can also be used to perform reconnaissance and surveillance, as a support platform for amphibious operations, and as a supply vessel for fuel and equipment used by their naval drones. According to the developers, the drone can perform these tasks 24/7 and in all weather conditions.
Russia’s military has sometimes struggled to contain Ukraine’s growing sea drone threat, deploying everything from advanced fighter jets to attack helicopters to block ships and shore-based machine guns to interdict Ukrainian robot boat attacks. In May 2025, Ukraine’s special operations command first fielded Maguras armed with anti-aircraft missiles. Russian official sources said the tactic was ineffective. Ukrainian sources said at least three helicopters were shot down before Russian air assets learned to keep a safe distance from the Ukrainian sea drones.
First shown to the public in July 2023, Ukraine’s Magura-series maritime drones operating in kamikaze mode have scored repeated naval successes and become a critical weapon in Kyiv’s increasingly effective campaign to disable or destroy warships of Russia’s Black Sea Fleet. The possibly most spectacular attack taking place on Feb. 1, 2024, saw six Maguras overwhelm shipboard defenses to sink the Tarantul-II covette Ivanovets within sight of shore of the Russia-controlled Crimea peninsula. Reportedly, 40 hands lost their lives. A Feb. 14, 2024, nocturnal strike scored multiple hits on and sank the 4,000-ton heavy assault ship Tsezar Kulikov offshore from the Crimea seaside resort Alupa.
Recent high-profile operations using Magura boats as FPV launch platforms include an early August 2026 strike by FPV drones flown from Maguras operating off the Crimea coast to hit a pair of Russian S-400 Triumf interceptor missile launchers and an air defense radar protecting the south shore of the peninsula. A Ukrainian defense intelligence (HUR) statement estimated the value of Russian equipment losses in excess of $50 million dollars. Other Ukrainian drone units, possibly assisted by the take-down of the S-400, touted by the Kremlin to be the world’s most advanced air defense system, struck at least 60 targets across Crimea in the weeks following the HUR air raid, Kyiv Post records showed.
The US-based military maritime equipment company RECONCRAFT and UFORCE, in July 2026, signed a memorandum of understanding for licensed production of Ukrainian Magura boats in Oregon and South Carolina, with the American boatbuilder providing manufacturing capability and UFORCE providing software, guidance systems and command-and-control technology. News reports have mentioned potential production volumes of hundreds of boats annually.
Current Ukrainian production of Magura boats is a military secret. According to open sources, Ukraine’s special forces and navy have almost certainly fielded at least 100 boats since first fielding them in 2023, and possibly as many as 300.
The US, Great Britain, Turkey and China have experimented with drones flown from conventional, human-operated aircraft carriers, but none of those countries has yet fielded an aircraft carrier-launched drone operationally. Iran converted the container ship Shahid Bahman Bagheri into a drone carrier equipped with a ski-jump launch ramp in the early 2020s. US and Israeli air strikes in February-March 2026 sank the vessel in shallow water near the Bandar Abbas/Khuran Strait.

The Vatican offered its “good offices” Tuesday to help achieve a settlement in the Russia-Ukraine war, saying it would continue supporting efforts to create space for dialogue.
Speaking at a joint news conference in Moscow with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher said the Vatican would continue supporting efforts to achieve a settlement.
 
Gallagher, the Vatican's secretary for relations with states, said it would contribute to and offer space for dialogue while continuing its charitable and humanitarian efforts.
“Indeed, we offer our good offices in any way that can help, in the hope that the much desired peace can be achieved as soon as possible,” Gallagher said.
“This is my sincere wish for the people of the Russian Federation, for the Ukrainian people, and all those who continue to suffer on account of this tragic war,” he added.
Gallagher expressed gratitude for what he described as a “frank and constructive” conversation with Lavrov.
He said the Ukraine war was among several topics they discussed and that, despite “substantial” differences and “numerous important points” of convergence, both sides reaffirmed the need to keep communication channels open.
Gallagher said the Vatican continued to follow the war with “deep concern.”
During his meeting with Lavrov, Gallagher said he reiterated Pope Leo XIV’s appeal to end hostilities and begin “authentic negotiations with the support of the international community.”
“The position of the Holy See remains clear. The conflict cannot be resolved by military means. It is essential to create the conditions for a serious political and diplomatic process,” he said.
Gallagher urged Moscow and Kyiv to “demonstrate openness and goodwill so that such dialogue can become a reality.” He also reiterated the need to respect international humanitarian law.
“Peace must be founded on the full respect of international law and of the principles of the Charter of the United Nations,” he added.
For his part, Lavrov said he conveyed Moscow’s gratitude to the Vatican for what he described as its balanced position on the situation in and around Ukraine.
 
“We outlined Russia's principled approaches to resolving the Ukrainian crisis by addressing its root causes and reaffirmed our appreciation for the Vatican's active engagement in resolving a number of pressing humanitarian issues within the conflict in Ukraine,” Lavrov said.
Lavrov said Russia and the Vatican maintained a trusting relationship and that Moscow supported efforts to inject new momentum into inter-church dialogue.
He also expressed hope that Vatican officials would pay attention to issues raised by Russia in their contacts with the Ukrainian side.
Lavrov said he informed Gallagher of Russia's readiness to resume political consultations at the deputy foreign minister level.
He added that Moscow was also ready to resume “targeted” consultations between the two sides' ministries on specific issues at the expert level.

Two UN peacekeepers killed in South Sudan
